title: Goal 1's interval p95 is set by the platform's vsync tick, not by late frames (no lever in the app)
body:
## Summary
Every active window of both muted runs is over 16.7 ms on jitter alone; SF's own VSYNC-app tick has an interval p95 of 16.736-16.739 ms.

## Description
The I2 p95 reads render-start intervals. The app renders on SF's VSYNC-app timer, which ticks every 16.679 ms (fitted 16.6795; the display mode is 59.94 Hz, SF's present grid 16.68335 ms). 16.7 ms is 0.02 ms above that period, so any start that lands 0.02 ms later than the one before counts. 27.4% of the tick intervals themselves exceed 16.7 ms (4,494 ticks in three whole 25 s traces).

## Flow
No change. Goes to the owner as a question under decisions section 10(c): the bar stays.

## Expected impact
The whole window p95: measured worst 19.044 / 19.388 ms; with every on-time interval over 16.7 ms set to one refresh, 16.689 / 16.686 ms and 0 of 240 / 248 windows over.

## Evaluation
Rank 1 of 12 by P17's attribution.
Claim: Class (a) jitter alone keeps the window p95 over 16.7 ms.
Before: worst window p95 19.044 / 19.388 ms; 240 of 240 and 248 of 248 windows over 16.7 ms on class (a) alone
After: n/a (no change)
Method: perf-p17.py windows rebuilt on the device clock (235 of 240 and 244 of 248 match their own count), SF present intervals; perf-p17-trace.py VSYNC-app ticks
Result: declined: no lever; owner question
Gate: none (no change)

title: Render start waits on the main thread's Choreographer callback (tick to callback p95 2.4-2.5 ms)
body:
## Summary
Between SF's VSYNC-app tick and the render start, the app main thread's callback lag is the largest varying part.

## Description
Trace split of each start: tick -> main-thread wakeup 0.12 ms (p95 0.17); wakeup -> run p50 0.04, p95 1.93-2.01 ms (CPUs held first by surfaceflinger (RT), whose composition wakes at the same tick, then by the link threads); run -> callback p50 0.20-0.22, p95 0.90-2.11 ms; GL wakeup -> run p50 0.21-0.23 ms. Across intervals over 16.7 ms, vsync-to-start grows by 0.56-0.92 ms on average, 0.17-0.48 ms of it in the callback lag. In muted-run1, 1,335 of the 8,806 on-time intervals over 16.7 ms sit in a second mode at +1.25-1.75 ms over the period.

## Flow
Perf arm first: request the frame from a dedicated thread's Choreographer at display priority (a HandlerThread looper), so SF's composition and the main thread's other work no longer sit between the tick and requestRendering. The cadence stays the vsync's and the render code is unchanged. A/B against main on window p95, pooled p95, frames over 20 ms and SF present intervals.

## Expected impact
It can narrow the jitter, not bring the p95 under 16.7 ms (card 1: the tick's own p95 is 16.736 ms). Ceiling: the second jitter mode (1,335 intervals in run 1).

## Evaluation
Rank 2 of 12 by P17's attribution.
Claim: Moving the callback off the main thread lowers the share of intervals over 16.7 ms and the window p95.
Before: tick to callback p50 0.38-0.40, p95 2.36-2.52 ms; worst window p95 19.044 / 19.388 ms
After: not built
Method: perf-p17-trace.py mainThreadCallback and startDelay (three whole 25 s traces of diag-muted)
Result: open. Decisions section 11 ruling 3: within N3 and I2's clocks rule as a perf-only arm in dev.deathride.perf (the vsync cadence, game clock, input rate and every threshold stay); not scheduled before the owner's answer on goal 1's measure, because under any answer it cannot change goal 1's verdict (the tick's own p95 is 16.736 ms)
Gate: settled A/B pair under a rule fixed first; nothing a player sees or hears changes; :game:test

title: Buffer back-pressure: the GL thread sleeps 8-9 ms in dequeueBuffer (the largest cause of frames over 20 ms)
body:
## Summary
sleep:dequeue leads the frames over 20 ms: 12 of 38 (run 1), 21 of 77 (run 2), 29 of 95 (diag).

## Description
Of the 16 active frames over 20 ms in the three traces, 6 slept 8-9.6 ms in dequeueBuffer, woken by SurfaceFlinger's binder thread (Binder:424) or an unnamed task: the next buffer was not yet released. 3 more ran long with 6.2-8.0 ms of dequeue sleep beside it. The profile's sleep:dequeue label also holds lock sleeps that only the trace separates (2 on ART's JIT code cache lock, 1 on the ClassLinker lock; the JIT and GC cards). The phases: in run 2 the whole foundry round sat in back-pressure (clear median 6.55 ms against 0.65 ms in the other rounds; work 15.29 ms), and run 2 and diag put these frames on foundry and salt. GPU time (frameReady - queue) at those frames: median 6.5 / 9.1 / 5.9 ms. Per round, GPU time ran 9.0-10.1 ms on foundry and salt in some rounds against 5.5-7.0 ms elsewhere, but not in every round. All but one of them presented on the next refresh (class a).

## Flow
Research first: name the lever before any change. Add a perf-only reading of the buffer queue (SF latch and release per frame) beside GPU time per course, on a settled pair. One lever to test is a pixel-identical GPU cut on foundry and salt; none is assumed.

## Expected impact
Worst window p95 without these frames: 19.044 -> 18.857 ms (run 1), 19.388 -> 19.302 ms (run 2); no window crosses 16.7 ms. Frames over 20 ms: -12 / -21.

## Evaluation
Rank 3 of 12 by P17's attribution.
Claim: A pixel-identical change removes the back-pressure phases.
Before: sleep:dequeue 12 / 21 / 29 frames over 20 ms; worst window effect -0.187 / -0.086 ms
After: not built
Method: perf-p17.py cause (schedstat split, clear and swap excess); perf-p17-trace.py traceDetail (dequeueBuffer the largest contributor in 6 of 16 traced frames)
Result: open (lever not named)
Gate: pixel diff 0 on the Stick; GPU ms; frames over 20 ms; window p95; settled pair

title: Preemption of the render thread by platform threads (no app lever)
body:
## Summary
preempted leads 11 of 38 / 11 of 77 / 23 of 95 frames over 20 ms; the CPU went to platform threads.

## Description
Runnable wait in those frames averages 2.3 ms (median interval 0.12 ms). In the traces the render thread was preempted by SurfaceFlinger's RT threads (its 'app' and 'sf' vsync EventThreads, Binder:424), the Wi-Fi driver's hif_thread (nice -10), the IME process (nice -10), kworkers and rcu_preempt. The app's own link threads (nice 13) never preempted it. The audio pair was idle (muted: AudioOut_D and writer 0.0% of a core).

## Flow
No change: the holders are platform threads above the render thread's priority.

## Expected impact
Worst window p95 without them: 19.044 -> 18.871 ms (run 1), unchanged in run 2; no window crosses 16.7 ms.

## Evaluation
Rank 4 of 12 by P17's attribution.
Claim: An app change removes the preemption.
Before: 11 / 11 / 23 frames over 20 ms
After: n/a
Method: schedWaitMs excess (perf-p17.py), trace preemptedBy
Result: declined: no lever
Gate: none

title: PSS line: the Java heap swing is ART's 24 MB headroom; the probe's /profile reply was the largest app allocator and is served in place (built, kept)
body:
## Summary
At each muted run's PSS peak the Java heap is 7-27 MiB above the lowest sample; graphics (52.0-52.1 MiB) and native heap (9.6-10.2) stay flat.

## Description
PSS 159.9-172.1 MiB in run 1 (peak at the first sample, after the /routes warm-up), 160.2-184.8 in run 2 (peak at 336 s: Java heap 77.2 MiB, +27.1) and 167.2-182.8 in diag (peak at 300 s: Java heap 73.8, +15.1). The process allocates 2.59 MB/s muted, with 35-38 GCs per 360 s run and none blocking. All are under 192 MiB here; P16's base-run2 read 194.3 with sound on (ruling 3).

## Flow
Built (P18): ART's own allocation tracker sampled a 360 s race over DDMS (perf-p18-alloc.py, 67 race windows, 524,322 records). Two thirds of a race's allocation is the probe's own HTTP reads: ktor CIO's 16 KB header-line buffers 36% (engine, section 7 ruling 2: reported, not changed), the /profile reply 20%, /stats 11%; the phones' websocket 18%, the game loop 8% (core 10%, game 10%, audio 1%, HUD/font 0.1% of all). The largest allocator in game/ or link/ was /profile (RaceServer.kt:180 10.2% + PerfTrace.json 9.5%): 3.4-4.0 MB of large char/byte arrays per 10 s read. It is now formatted in pieces into pooled 8 KiB UTF-8 blocks with the same bytes (293f77a0, ProfileReplyTest 5 cases).

## Expected impact
Allocation -0.32 to -0.35 MB/s (-12.7%) under the profiled probe; GCs 35 -> 33, logged (long) GCs 22/20 -> 11/11. The PSS peak is not expected to fall with the rate: after every logged full GC in all five P18 runs ART set the footprint exactly 24 MB above what survived (48-59 MB surviving, footprint 72-83 MB), and the heap fills that headroom before the next GC whatever the rate. The PSS line goes to a settled pair or the next goal-1 soak.

## Evaluation
Rank 5 of 12 by P17's attribution.
Claim: The largest allocator in game/ or link/ can be cut in place with the same output, and the cut allocates less.
Before: base 2.599 / 2.576 MB/s, 35 / 35 GCs; PSS max 181.99 / 168.06 MiB (Java heap at the peak 75.2 / 59.3)
After: cut 2.271 / 2.254 MB/s, 33 / 33 GCs; PSS max 181.87 / 186.56 MiB (Java heap at the peak 73.0 / 73.7)
Method: perf-p18.py's rule (70fe350c, fixed before the first A/B run); four interleaved profiled 360 s runs, default sound arm; two 900 s settle waits never settled, so the four runs are research
Result: built, kept by the rule (equivalence green AND both cut runs allocate less than both base runs); the PSS line is not graded (unsettled); no-regression readings: frames over 33 ms 68 / 96 base, 84 / 95 cut; worst active p95 25.145 / 26.888 base, 24.603 / 26.721 cut; rejected inputs 0 in all four
Gate: gradlew :core:test :link:test :game:test green (core 261, link 34 with 2 skipped, game 117); assembleRelease passed

title: Re-grade P16 card 1 (one HUD font page) for its memory: font textures 5 -> 2 MiB
body:
## Summary
Ruling 1: card 1 comes back ranked by P17. Its value is memory (GL mtrack -3 MiB), not the tail.

## Description
P16 figures: HUD flushes 3 -> 2 per active frame, hudDraws 6 -> 5, font textures 5 -> 2 MiB (owned 39.97 -> 36.97), text diff 0 in 6 Stick captures, hudMs not shown (fonts 1.166 / 1.616 ms against base 1.182 / 1.183). P17 gives the HUD no share of the p95: setting the running:hud frames over 20 ms (5 / 2 / 9) to one refresh moves no worst window. Its PSS angle: graphics is flat at 52 MiB, so -3 MiB is a fixed cut of the PSS peak. P16's base-run2 at 194.3 MiB (sound on) would read about 191.3.

## Flow
Re-land 12390e79 + feebc1ff (the font page) on a perf arm and re-grade it with a settled pair, under a new rule fixed before the first graded run that names PSS max beside hudMs.

## Expected impact
PSS max about -3 MiB; hudMs not expected to show.

## Evaluation
Rank 6 of 12 by P17's attribution.
Claim: PSS max falls by about 3 MiB with no pixel change.
Before: P16: owned textures 39.97 MiB; PSS max 174.9-194.3 MiB (sound on)
After: not re-run
Method: P16 evidence (evidence/perf/p16) and P17 attribution
Result: open
Gate: settled pair; the rule names PSS max and hudMs; text diff 0

title: ART JIT code cache lock: 11-15 ms render-thread sleeps on the debuggable perf build
body:
## Summary
2 of the 16 traced frames over 20 ms slept 11.0 and 14.7 ms on ART's JIT code cache lock, woken by ART's Profile Saver.

## Description
dev.deathride.perf is debuggable (the audio arms need it), so ART runs it JIT-only; the shipped package gets ahead-of-time code from its profile. The profile's rule names these frames sleep:dequeue (their flush/swap excess is large too); only the trace separates them. Whether the shipped build carries this tail is not measured.

## Flow
Measure the muted tail on a non-debuggable profiled build with the same probe (the profile flag works on any build; the muted arm needs a way to mute that does not depend on the debuggable gate, which is the App Master's call).

## Expected impact
Up to 2 of 16 traced frames over 20 ms; no window p95 effect expected.

## Evaluation
Rank 7 of 12 by P17's attribution.
Claim: The JIT lock sleeps belong to the debuggable perf build only.
Before: 2 of 16 traced frames over 20 ms (11.0 and 14.7 ms sleeps), none over 33 ms, no window moved
After: n/a
Method: perf-p17-trace.py traceDetail
Result: declined by decisions section 11 ruling 4 (no mute path outside the debuggable gate: a mute that works in a non-debuggable build is a sound control in a build a player could run, N3's ground)
Gate: none

title: On-CPU spikes spread over the phases (cars, HUD, simulation, scenery, flush)
body:
## Summary
running:<phase> causes 15 of 38 / 42 of 77 / 40 of 95 frames over 20 ms, spread over five phases.

## Description
Run 1: hud 5, simulation 4, cars 3, flushSwap 3. Run 2: cars 30, simulation 6, hud 2, scenery 2, flushSwap 2; 25 of those 42 fell in the foundry round's back-pressure phase (render thread on-CPU 14-17 ms against a 9.3 ms median). Diag: cars 19, hud 9, scenery 5, simulation 3, flushSwap 3, telemetry 1. No phase does a different job in those frames. The cause cannot be separated with these readings, which hold no CPU or GPU frequency record.

## Flow
No single change; the foundry phase is part of card 3's research.

## Expected impact
Worst window without running:cars: 19.044 -> 18.974 ms (run 1), unchanged (run 2). Without each other phase: no change.

## Evaluation
Rank 8 of 12 by P17's attribution.
Claim: One phase change moves the tail.
Before: 15 / 42 / 40 frames over 20 ms
After: n/a
Method: schedRunMs excess with P11's dominant phase
Result: declined: no lever named
Gate: none

title: The probe's /stats load beside slow frames (observer effect, below the p95's resolution)
body:
## Summary
A /stats build fell inside 3 of 38 / 3 of 77 / 4 of 95 frames over 20 ms, against 1.5% of all active intervals.

## Description
That is 2.6-5x the base rate. The app's link threads ran at 39-47% of a core over each run (DefaultDispatcher, nice 13) and never preempted the render thread in the traces. Wi-Fi sent 477-564 KB/s. Players' phones never read /stats; decisions section 7 ruling 2 keeps the cadence for comparability.

## Flow
No change (section 7 ruling 2).

## Expected impact
At most 4 frames over 20 ms a run; no window crosses 16.7 ms.

## Evaluation
Rank 9 of 12 by P17's attribution.
Claim: The /stats load causes frames over 20 ms.
Before: 3 / 3 / 4 frames
After: n/a
Method: each window's uptimeMs on the device clock against each interval
Result: declined: observer effect, kept for comparability

title: ART GC overlap with slow frames (a third of the traced ones; no window moves)
body:
## Summary
A logged GC overlapped 4 of 38 / 5 of 77 / 4 of 95 frames over 20 ms and the profile's rule names sleep:gc for 0 / 2 / 0; the trace sees a concurrent GC in 5 of its 16.

## Description
35 / 38 GCs per run at 2.59 MB/s, none blocking; ART logs only the long ones, so the profile undercounts the overlap. In the traces, 5 of the 16 active frames over 20 ms overlapped a concurrent GC (37-95 ms long). In 3 of them the render thread slept on a lock the GC held (the large-object-space lock 4.2-4.7 ms twice, the ClassLinker lock once), but only the ClassLinker one was the frame's largest contributor; the other 4 ran long.

## Flow
No change beyond card 5.

## Expected impact
Worst window without the sleep:gc frames: unchanged.

## Evaluation
Rank 10 of 12 by P17's attribution.
Claim: GC causes the muted tail.
Before: sleep:gc 0 / 2 / 0
After: n/a
Method: logcat GC lines on the profile clock; trace sleepBy
Result: declined: share too small to move a window
Gate: none

title: Class (b) 'missed refreshes' in SF's present times are a model beat, not missed frames
body:
## Summary
90 / 82 active present intervals of two refreshes, balanced by 94 / 85 of zero, came in bursts every ~72 s; SF's own missed-frame counters read 0.

## Description
SF's present times lie on an exact 16,683,350 ns grid (residual 0 ns over each run): a model, not measured fences. SF composes on its VSYNC-sf timer every 16.679 ms. Render starts drift through the grid at -0.11 to -0.15 ms/s, and each time they cross the refresh boundary a burst of 0/2 pairs follows. Those frames' render intervals average 16.6-17.0 ms. In the three traces, which held 48 class (b) frames, SF counted 0 missed frames (PrevFrameMissed, PrevHwcFrameMissed, PrevGpuFrameMissed) in 4,496 compositions.

## Flow
No change. The present-time source's limit is recorded: software on this Stick cannot read the real panel's cadence.

## Expected impact
None on the p95 (class (b) removed: worst 19.057 / 19.388 ms).

## Evaluation
Rank 11 of 12 by P17's attribution.
Claim: The display missed refreshes.
Before: 90 / 82 class (b)
After: n/a
Method: SF --latency grid residual; trace SF counters
Result: declined: an artifact of the present model
Gate: none
